doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

chapter: Synths, the section and stopping playing
title: No longer playing; arranging took over
summary: Hey stopped playing about ten years ago; arranging got him in the door but drew focus from trumpet, and health issues followed.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I see. Do you miss — are you still playing?
No. I haven’t been for I don’t know, it’s been ten years at least.
Yeah. Do you miss it that much?

Oh God, terribly. If I could play and not arrange I would take playing. But the playing of the arranging got us in as a section more than my playing did. So you know that’s, the good news is that I can do this arranging and Quincy would call me to do the arranging, he wouldn’t call me to do the playing, but because I was arranging I was playing. And then he found out that we could play but you know, so the arranging kind of got my foot more in the door than the playing I think. So it’s, you know, it’s kind of a curse of, it’s part of the reason that I’m not playing anymore because I was so involved in the arranging that you have to worry about whether everybody’s playing in tune, whether the cut-off was right, whether we’re in time, whether the producer likes the horn parts, whether the engineer has a horrible sound on the trombone and we have to re-play the whole song, which we have done many times. You know there are so many other aspects to arranging for me that I want to make it sound like I know it should sound that it took away from my trumpet playing. So you know my focus was on the arranging and not on the playing. And it was always easy for me to go in originally — I could play anything. I mean literally play anything. So I could put my focus over there. But you know, the older you get, you know the harder trumpet gets, and then the focus still has to be over here to make sure that we’re still sounding like we should sound, and the trumpet kind of started going downhill because of that. And then I had some health issues.
